title: Send more email only to people who read it
subtitle: In a 12-week, 450,000-subscriber cadence test, going from 2 to 4 emails a week raised revenue by 21%. Going to 6 added almost nothing, burned through the list and cost us revenue once the test ended. A cadence set by engagement beats any single frequency.
summary: We randomised 450,000 email subscribers to 2, 4 or 6 promotional emails a week for 12 weeks. Four a week lifted revenue per recipient by 21% over two. Six a week added no significant revenue, tripled unsubscribes and earned less once the test ended. We recommend an engagement-based cadence (6/4/2 by tier), worth an estimated +$4.6M a year with no more unsubscribes than today.
key_findings: Going from 2 to 4 emails a week lifted 12-week revenue per recipient by +$0.85 (+21%, 95% CI +$0.61 to +$1.09). Going from 4 to 6 added only +$0.17 (not significant).
Unsubscribes rose from 1.9% at 2/wk to 6.1% at 6/wk. Weekly clickers in the 6/wk arm fell by a third over 12 weeks.
Over 21 weeks including follow-up, 4/wk ($8.43) beat 6/wk ($8.17), and 6/wk earned 15% less than 2/wk after the test.
High-engagement subscribers (22% of the list) earned the most at 6/wk. Lapsed subscribers (47%) earned the least at 6/wk and 8.6% of them unsubscribed.
An engagement-based 6/4/2 cadence is modelled at +15% revenue per recipient, or about +$4.6M a year, with flat unsubscribes.
